items.contract: The administrator imports an initial definition or exact accepted baseline; the workspace validates it, identifies the state, durably stores it, and opens that state.
rules: RULE-7 requires accepted baseline import to be atomic.
RULE-9 makes packaged kernel verify authoritative.
items.actorBoundary: Real local browser and Spring HTTP application backed by PostgreSQL 18.6 and packaged School Kernel
items.claim: Both explicit import modes and the exact accepted archive complete through the actor boundary and persist the corresponding lifecycle state.

evidence.observation: POST of the real definition returns 200; assertions compare INITIAL_DRAFT, no accepted timetable, supplied school displayName, import mode, ETag, version 1, one kernel invocation, and the complete stored definition tree.
POST of a definition and packaged-plan result returns 200; assertions compare ACCEPTED_BASELINE and both complete stored JSON trees.
A visible browser imported examples/initial-school.json and rendered Initial draft, No accepted timetable, Demo School, and the exact definition revision with zero console errors or warnings.

items.contract: A result alone is rejected with a matching-definition explanation and no import.
rules: RULE-22 requires safe stable failure output.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP import route
items.claim: A result-only upload returns MATCHING_DEFINITION_REQUIRED and leaves the exact empty aggregate.

evidence.observation: Assertions require HTTP 422, code MATCHING_DEFINITION_REQUIRED, no assignments text, EMPTY, version 0, {} JSONB, and zero kernel invocations.

items.contract: An accepted archive must contain exactly the three safe root entries; absent, duplicate, extra, unreadable, or unsafe content rejects the import.
rules: RULE-14 defines exact bounded no-extraction ZIP parsing.
items.actorBoundary: Multipart HTTP import and bounded archive reader
items.claim: Exact archives import; missing, duplicate, extra, directory, traversal, separator, encrypted, unreadable, truncated, dishonest-length, and oversized forms are rejected without mutation or extraction.

evidence.observation: The exact archive reaches ACCEPTED_BASELINE; a traversal archive returns 422 UNSAFE_ARCHIVE and the row remains exactly empty.
The real HTTP matrix rejects missing, duplicate, encrypted, invalid-signature, and oversized archives with exact safe codes, empty state, and zero kernel invocations.
The complete malformed archive corpus and exact byte boundaries are read in memory without extraction.

items.contract: Parsing, version, identity, revision, assignment, hard-validity, or lineage failure names a safe reason and persists or discloses nothing.
rules: RULE-26 requires the independent direct hard-feasibility verifier.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged verify process followed by real HTTP import
items.claim: Strict kernel verification rejects malformed, unsupported, mismatched, incomplete, tampered, and hard-invalid documents before workspace mutation.

evidence.observation: Packaged verify rejects unsupported schema/catalog, missing/blank school name, successor-only, wrong school/revision, incomplete assignment set, collision, and unknown room with INVALID_INPUT, no timetable, and no solver start.
The direct production verifier rejects an independently constructed mutation for every one of the ten hard constraints.
The complete definition/baseline matrix is repeated through real HTTP; each response is safe 422, state remains exactly empty, and only verify is invoked.

items.contract: Definition-only import containing basedOnRevision is rejected without state change.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged School Kernel verify process followed by real HTTP import
items.claim: Successor-only input returns INVALID_INPUT and cannot reach persistence.

evidence.observation: Successor-only input returns structured INVALID_INPUT through packaged verify and real HTTP, with exact empty state and no persistence.

items.contract: A definition/result import requires a complete FEASIBLE result matching the exact definition.
rules: RULE-9 baseline mode requires exact definition revision and direct hard validity.
items.actorBoundary: Packaged verify process and accepted-pair HTTP route
items.claim: Only an exact complete verified pair becomes ACCEPTED_BASELINE.

evidence.observation: A packaged-plan FEASIBLE result verifies with definitionRevision and timetableRevision equal by value.
The verified pair is stored atomically as the complete accepted definition, result, and manifest.

items.contract: Durable-storage failure reports incomplete import, exposes no accepted baseline, and leaves the workspace empty.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP and PostgreSQL transaction with injected trigger failure
items.claim: Statement, deferred-commit, connection-termination, and restart boundaries preserve all-or-nothing durable state.

evidence.observation: Independent statement, deferred-commit, and connection-termination failures return safe 503 and preserve canonical empty state; a durable accepted bundle survives a fresh application context byte-equivalently.

items.contract: Definition-only creates a draft; verified pair creates an accepted baseline; invalid input is never current.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP import representations and PostgreSQL state
items.claim: Import modes have distinct durable lifecycle and acceptedTimetable values.

evidence.observation: Definition mode asserts INITIAL_DRAFT and acceptedTimetable false; accepted-pair mode asserts ACCEPTED_BASELINE and true.

items.contract: Identifiers are exact and names, weekdays, ordering, and optional times come from metadata rather than ID spelling.
rules: RULE-8 forbids reconstructing kernel documents or interpreting IDs.
items.actorBoundary: Stored JSONB snapshot and native browser presentation
items.claim: The complete imported document is retained by value and the browser renders only the required definition-supplied school displayName, never schoolId as a heading.

evidence.observation: Tests compare the complete stored definition and Unicode/omitted-field canonical form, and assert the stored school displayName exactly.
Real headless Chrome imports the fixture, asserts heading Demo School, and explicitly rejects demo-school and the old unavailable-name fallback text.
Visible Playwright journey renders Demo School from metadata and the exact definition revision with zero console errors/warnings.

items.contract: Without a manifest, imported locks are persistent policy.

items.claim: Every imported period/room lock is recorded with PERSISTENT_POLICY origin.

items.contract: Validation is isolated and accepts no unsupported schema or catalog version.

items.claim: Every import journey uses isolated state and strict versioned schemas.

evidence.observation: Required school name and unsupported/coercive versions are rejected by the strict schema pipeline.
Unsupported schema/catalog and school-name cases are rejected through the actor boundary on disposable PostgreSQL 18.6.

items.contract: Rejected or interrupted import persists no partial state and makes data unavailable beyond the local machine.

Virtual-thread interruption returns KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE, preserves interrupt status, destroys the child, emits only safe summary logging, and leaves the private root empty.

items.contract: Success leaves exactly one durable initial draft or verified accepted baseline.

items.claim: Both successful modes leave version 1 and exactly the corresponding complete document state.

evidence.observation: Definition and accepted-pair tests assert lifecycle, version, complete JSON values, and durable restart restoration.

items.contract: Failure leaves the workspace empty and discloses or accepts no candidate timetable.
items.actorBoundary: Real HTTP failure responses and PostgreSQL row
items.claim: All import refusal families assert the canonical empty row and candidate absence.

evidence.observation: Every archive, verification, malformed-request, lifecycle, and storage failure family asserts exact prior state, safe response, no candidate, and zero prohibited process invocation where applicable.

items.contract: Kernel inputs are byte/token/depth bounded and atomic publication is exactly-one without force and replacement with force.
